title: WebSockets Quick Reference
description: Look up a lesson idea, see its small example, and check a common mistake. Open the linked lesson for setup and practice steps.

entries.name: Receive a welcome message
entries.summary: The server sends text when a client connects. The client reads one message and closes.
notes: A WebSocket server must be listening before a client can connect.

entries.name: Send from the client
entries.summary: The open event means the connection is ready. Sending before it is ready can fail.
notes: Wait for open before calling send.

entries.name: Return the same message
entries.summary: An echo server sends received text back unchanged.
notes: Node ws receives Buffer data by default; turn text into a string.

entries.name: Send structured message data
entries.summary: JSON can give a message named fields. The server reads score and doubles it.
notes: Real message handlers need checks for invalid JSON and invalid fields.

entries.name: Check a message shape
entries.summary: A parsed object may still be missing a field. This example sends an empty object and gets a clear reply.
notes: Parsing JSON and checking its field types are separate jobs.

entries.name: Send to connected clients
entries.summary: A broadcast visits each connected client. Only open sockets are ready to send.
notes: A disconnected socket is not ready for a send.

entries.name: Check connection state
entries.summary: readyState reports the current state. Inside open, it equals WebSocket.OPEN.
notes: The connection can close later, so readiness is not a permanent promise.

entries.name: Receive bytes
entries.summary: A binary message carries bytes rather than text. This server sends three small byte values.
notes: Do not decode arbitrary binary bytes as if they were normal text.

entries.name: Check that a peer responds
entries.summary: Ping and pong are control messages. The ws client automatically answers a ping with pong.
notes: A real heartbeat needs a timeout for peers that never answer.

entries.name: Close with a reason
entries.summary: A close frame can carry a code and short reason. Code 1000 means a normal close.
notes: A close event means messages can no longer be sent on that connection.

entries.name: Handle unreadable JSON
entries.summary: JSON.parse can fail. A catch block sends a friendly reply instead of crashing this handler.
notes: Catch the parse failure and then check the parsed data shape separately.

entries.name: Limit message size
entries.summary: maxPayload limits incoming message bytes. The client sends five bytes to a server limited to four.
notes: Keep limits clear; a message that is too large is closed with a protocol size error.
